kind: Unregistered diagnostic; this is not evidence for a release gate
question: Why did the bounded GET-only Google adapter-versus-mount validator find no comparable file in the second active My Drive connection?
privacy: The run emitted only aggregate counts and byte totals. Account labels, identities, item IDs, paths, names, hashes, tokens and provider bodies were not recorded.

initial_result.classification: The connection had no eligible ordinary file at or below the fixed one-MiB validator limit. This was a harness boundary, not a provider or mount failure.

corrections.problem: The first-account diagnostic selected generated Google browser-link projections when their collision-safe projected names did not end in .url.
corrections.cause: The harness classified generated links by filename suffix instead of provider-neutral typed metadata.
corrections.change: Select only ordinary files with no shortcut target or package marker and with both a mutation precondition and content revision.

corrections.problem: The first-account diagnostic initially reported eight indexed content and metadata changes although the mounted reads were current.
corrections.cause: The harness queried only the completed nodes baseline and ignored newer foreground observations and observed absence records used by the mounted namespace.
corrections.change: Read the effective visible store view by overlaying foreground observations on the completed baseline and filtering observed absences.

change_under_test.description: Keep the one-MiB default but accept an explicit per-file limit from 1 byte through 64 MiB.
change_under_test.invalid_limit_check: 67108865 bytes was refused before a live read.

isolated_upgrade_probe: A private, mutation-free current-daemon probe over a copied legacy baseline reached ready and read an exact bounded file through the isolated mount. Foreground observations overlaid the legacy baseline, confirming that raw nodes-table inspection was not the mounted view. No account, item, path or content identifiers are recorded here.
interpretation: For these ten exact ordinary files across two active connections, the direct Google adapter bytes and mounted bytes matched after correcting the diagnostic. The result does not establish arbitrary-file reliability, provider-wide correctness or a release gate because its question and prediction were not registered before the run.
